text:
leo: FYI rolled out dyn-batcher-kv-evict v1 to low-latency clusters this morning.

leo: quick summary: p95 down ~20% for conversational routes with typical prefixes, median roughly the same, and token compute across the sampled workload down ~12%.

mira: nice! what's the canary math?

leo: canary (90m): baseline p95 = 310ms -> v1 p95 = 248ms. p50 = 38ms -> 37ms. observed request coalescing rate up from 18% -> 44% for eligible traffic.

chris: which routes/models are eligible? any exclusions?

leo: eligible = routes with seq <= 96 and prefix_kv_enabled. Excluded streaming-only, long-context, and routes that opted into "latency-first". Models: rwd-chat-small, rwd-chat-medium, hosted-gg-7b, hosted-llama2-7b.

rin: what changed technically?

leo: two parts: (1) eviction-aware KV compatibility check so we avoid coalescing requests that would trigger expensive KV re-materialization, (2) dynamic microbatch cap based on incoming QPS and recent tail. Also a conservative fast-path that skips coalesce if predicted tail risk > 0.6.

leo: config we flipped:
```
batching.strategy = "dynamic"
batching.max_microbatch = 8
kv.eviction_threshold = 0.12
kv.compatibility_check = "fast-approx"
```

mira: any incidents during canary?

leo: we saw one short regression on a high-variance tenant causing p95 blips (~+10%) for 5 mins; root cause was an unusual prefix churn pattern. Mitigated by temporary pinning that tenant to latency-first routing.

ops-bot: canary: dyn-batcher-kv-evict v1 promoted to region-eu-central at 2026-12-14T08:40:12Z :white_check_mark:

chris: alerts we should watch? dashboards?

leo: dashboards: https://dashboards.redwood.com/d/dynbatch/kv-evict-v1 
runbook: https://wiki.redwood.com/runbooks/dyn-batcher-kv-evict 
New alerts: batch.coalesce.rate.drop and kv.eviction.rehydra.count. Added a circuit-breaker to auto-fallback to fixed-batching if coalesce.rate < 5% for >3m.

mira: will customers see anything?

leo: no API change. performance policy tweak: default for seq<=96 is now "cost-balanced-dynamic". Customers that need pure tail latency can set `route.performance_policy = \"latency-priority\"`.

rin: please file a short note for #announcements and add to the weekly chime. good win. :tada:

leo: already prepping a one-paragraph blurb, will post in #announcements and product channels.

chris: follow-ups: ticket 5152 (dashboard opt-out count), 5153 (tenant pinning automation), 5154 (kv rehydration telemetry improvements).

leo: thanks to runtime + infra + sres teams for quick testing. closing thread 1
